solutions.title: DFS clone with map
solutions.strategy: Recursively clone each discovered node and store the original-to-copy mapping before traversing neighbors.

timeComplexity.explanation: Every node is cloned once and every neighbor reference is inspected once.

spaceComplexity.explanation: The clone map stores one entry per node, and recursion can hold up to V stack frames in a chain-shaped graph.

solutions.title: BFS clone with queue
solutions.strategy: Use a queue to discover nodes iteratively, creating clones on first sight and appending cloned neighbors in fixture order.

timeComplexity.explanation: Queue processing visits every node once and scans all adjacency entries.

spaceComplexity.explanation: The map and queue store cloned or pending nodes proportional to the number of vertices.
